hotContext.criticalNews: Giga Berlin 4680 line is in early production (from May 12, 2026) with PR video on July 16; expanded 18 GWh full-scale still H1 2027. Texas dry-electrode 4680 for some Model Y packs already previously confirmed. No new yield or actual GWh metrics this week.

recentKeyChanges.title: Giga Berlin 4680 production video drops — early ramp PR, full scale still H1 2027
recentKeyChanges.description: On July 16, 2026, BASENOR reported Tesla released a short video of the 4680 cell line at Gigafactory Berlin (circulated via Sawyer Merritt on X the same day). The piece frames production as having begun May 12, 2026 — under ten weeks before the video — with full-scale expanded output still targeted only for H1 2027. Capacity narrative is unchanged: +$250M to raise the Berlin annual target from 8 GWh to 18 GWh (~$1.45B cumulative battery investment at the site). Dry Battery Electrode (DBE) for anode and cathode is restated as the manufacturing story, not a new process milestone. BASENOR also cites autoevolution that 'Made in Germany' Model Ys with locally produced 4680 cells are expected late Q3 2026 — a consumer timeline that remains single-source and unverified by Teslarati/TeslaNorth/Tesla IR this week. Applications for the JUNI x Tesla Battery Cell Giga Challenge (launched July 6) remain open through July 24, underscoring that manufacturing bottlenecks are still being crowdsourced. No new yield %, actual GWh output, or cost-per-kWh figures were published with the video.

positive_signals: Tesla publicly showed live 4680 cell-line footage from Giga Berlin (~10 weeks after May 12 production start)
Capacity target still stated at 18 GWh/year after the May $250M add-on (~200k–350k vehicles/year at pack-level estimates)
Dry electrode process for both anode and cathode continues to be presented as in use on the Berlin line
Near-term Model Y-with-Berlin-4680 claim (late Q3 2026) would be a real product milestone if it lands
negative_signals: Line is still in an early, accelerating phase — not a finished high-volume factory; full-scale expanded production only H1 2027
Video and recap recycle May 12 investment / 8→18 GWh targets; no verified yield, scrap rate, or actual GWh shipped this week
Cell Giga Challenge applications still open until July 24 — Tesla is still soliciting external fixes for materials, equipment, ops, automation, and AI bottlenecks
Electrek (July 7, corroboration): 4680 remains Tesla's most troubled manufacturing effort; opening the line to startups is a tacit admission of in-house gaps
Capacity target was doubled before cost-competitive, high-yield production has been publicly proven at Berlin scale
Original 2020 Berlin cell ambition was up to ~250 GWh; 18 GWh is a fraction of that vision after multi-year delay and IRA-driven US pivot
Model Y late-Q3 4680 claim rests on secondary reporting (autoevolution via BASENOR), not multi-source or official confirmation
